name: CHROMEWORKS Phantom Veil Stealth Ocular System
description:
The Phantom Veil is Chromeworks' answer to the professional surveillance and counter-surveillance market, packaging passive 4K retinal recording, multi-algorithm facial recognition, and active biometric scrambling into a unit visually indistinguishable from an unaugmented eye. The scrambling suite projects micro-distortion fields across the user's own facial geometry, defeating standard recognition systems at a 94% rated success rate against commercial-grade scanners. Low-light amplification brings performance to near-thermal clarity in darkness without the telltale glow of active sensors.

The Phantom Veil occupies a legally ambiguous zone — the recording and low-light functions are sold under a Licensed tier, but the biometric scrambling module technically constitutes identity-concealment hardware under Great Lakes law, pushing it into Restricted territory. Chromeworks sells the scrambler as a separate 'privacy module' to maintain plausible corporate deniability, but every installer knows exactly what the full kit is for.
installation_requirements: Licensed cybernetics clinic for base unit; scrambler module installation frequently performed off-books; neural privacy partition recommended
rejection_risk: Low — Chromeworks' neural integration is class-leading; scrambler module adds negligible biological load
maintenance: Facial recognition database updates monthly via encrypted Chromeworks server; scrambler field recalibration every 4 months; retinal storage wiped manually by user
side_effects: Facial recognition subsystem occasionally activates involuntarily, generating unsolicited identity profiles of strangers in the user's visual field
Biometric scrambler causes mild proprioceptive dissonance — users report a subtle wrongness when viewing their own reflection
Continuous passive recording creates documented psychological effects around authenticity and memory trust
Scrambler field visible as minor visual artifacts to other users running active AR overlays
cultural_context: The Phantom Veil is the open secret of Meridian's professional shadow economy — journalists, investigators, fixers, and corporate spies all run them, and the city's security apparatus has a complicated relationship with a product that's technically illegal but manufactured by a premium brand with serious Spire-tier lobbying power. Chromeworks markets the base unit aggressively in Tier 3-4 'personal privacy' campaigns while quietly ensuring the scrambler module documentation never appears in official catalogs. Street-level installers call the full kit 'getting veiled,' and it's considered a serious professional investment.
story_hooks: A Phantom Veil's 8TB retinal archive surfaces on the black market, containing months of footage from inside a Spire-tier corporate boardroom — the original owner is missing

The latest Chromeworks facial recognition update has a bug: it's misidentifying a specific face across hundreds of Veil users simultaneously, all flagging the same unknown individual as a high-priority target
An activist collective is being systematically hunted despite running Phantom Veils — someone has cracked the scrambler, and they need to know how before the next member disappears
